title: Verbs that carry direction
title_target: ទៅ និង មក — teuw neng mòòk
goal: Get around by every kind of transport — and understand ទៅ and មក, two verbs that attach to other verbs to show direction from the speaker's point of view.
bekal: use ទៅ and មក as direction markers after a verb
name vehicles and how you ride them
buy a bus ticket and ask about schedules
say how long a trip takes

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — The bus ticket counter for Battambang
dialogs.intro: Ani buys a ticket to Battambang to visit a friend. Count how many times ទៅ and មក attach to another verb — and notice that both show direction relative to the speaker, not to the place.

lines.text: [សួស្ដី|sua-sdey] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ចង់|chang] [ទិញ|teñ] [សំបុត្រ|sam-bot] [ទៅ|teuw] [បាត់ដំបង|bat-dam-baang]។

grammars.title: ⚠️ ទៅ and មក — direction seen from where the speaker stands
body: ទៅ (*teuw*) means "go" and មក (*mòòk*) means "come". But both also attach **after other verbs** to show direction — away from the speaker or toward the speaker. English does something similar with "bring" vs "take", but Khmer does it with almost any verb.

head: Khmer
Say it
Literally
Translation
rows: ត្រឡប់មកវិញ
ត្រឡប់ទៅវិញ

after: What matters isn't the destination but **where the speaker is standing**. If you're at home calling a friend, you say យកមក ("bring it here"). If you're at the office talking about home, you say យកទៅ.

⚠️ A typical mistake: using ទៅ for every kind of movement because it means "go". ផ្ញើទៅខ្ញុំ ("send-go to me") sounds impossible to Cambodian ears — the thing is obviously coming toward you, so it's មក.

grammars.title: Verb chains
body: Khmer can line up several verbs with no linking words at all. It sounds complicated, but it's a lot like casual English: "go buy tickets", "come see", "go get lunch".

head: Khmer
Say it
Literally
Translation
rows: ទៅទិញសំបុត្រ
ដើរទៅផ្សារ
ជិះម៉ូតូទៅធ្វើការ
យកសៀវភៅមកឲ្យខ្ញុំ

after: ⚠️ The order follows **the order of events**. First you take it, then you bring it over, then you hand it over — and the sentence is built in exactly that order. If you're unsure how to build a verb chain, ask yourself: what happens first?

grammars.title: How you travel: ជិះ, បើក, ដើរ
body: Khmer uses different verbs depending on whether you're driving or riding.

after: ⚠️ Notice the pair **ឡើង / ចុះ** — up and down. Both are also used for prices (ថ្លៃឡើង, prices go up) and for temperature. And the ចុះ you already know from Unit 6 in ចុះថ្លៃ ("lower the price") is exactly the same word.

blocks.title: Three things about traveling in Cambodia
items: **Intercity buses are much more comfortable than some people expect**, but the schedule often slips by an hour. Asking ចេញម៉ោងប៉ុន្មានពិតប្រាកដ? ("what time exactly does it leave?") is normal and not rude.
**Carry your passport for travel between provinces.** Some bus companies ask for your passport number when you buy a ticket, and there are occasional checks on the road.

⚠️ **Motorbike taxis and tuk-tuks: agree on the price before you get on, always.** Asking after you arrive is the fastest way to pay three times as much. Ride-hailing apps are also common in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, and their prices are fixed.
